pr.title: Take a merged pull request's outstanding suggestions into a follow-up pull request
pr.head: d457761fc014888969b6decd0a6a6b157be7ec34

summary: Projector's reviews can list suggestions: optional improvements the code is correct without, which never block a sign-off. The fix-pr skill, the fixer, decides each one, implementing it or deferring it. The watch daemon is the background process that polls pull requests and sends each subscribed agent session one-line events, such as MERGED when a pull request merges.

Before this change, a pull request could merge while suggestions on it were still owed: the owner merged a signed-off head before the fixer built them, or the fixer had deferred one as reaching beyond the change. The MERGED line only said to finish the fixer, so those suggestions were lost.

Now the MERGED line sends the fixer after them, and fix-pr gains a section that verifies each one against the base as it stands and builds the warranted ones as one follow-up pull request, without asking the owner first. A CLOSED line is unchanged, because a pull request closed without merging owes nothing.

Merged head listsFixer's action in the MERGED line
1 or more suggestionsrun fix-pr … to take the N suggestions its merged head lists into a follow-up pull request, then finish it
no suggestionhave subagent … take any suggestion it deferred into a follow-up pull request, then finish it
(closed, not merged)finish subagent …

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Suggestion: a P3 review item, listed in the review body, never a thread.
  • Fixer: the fix-<number> or fix-stack-<number> subagent that runs fix-pr.
  • Deferred: a suggestion the fixer chose not to build on the pull request, recorded only in its report.

groups.title: The MERGED line counts what is owed
groups.kicker: The watch daemon words the fixer's closing action from the merged head's suggestions
intro: When a pull request merges, the daemon now counts the suggestions its last head lists and picks one of three wordings for the fixer's action. A count above zero says to run fix-pr on the pull request, which also starts a fixer when none ran. A count of zero still asks the fixer to take any suggestion it deferred on an earlier head, because only the fixer remembers those.
The count goes in the fixer's action, not the detail before the dash, because a reviewer subscribed to the same pull request hears that detail too.

files.note: merged_suggestions counts the merged head's suggestions; closing_actions words the fixer's action from that count.

checks.text: merged_suggestions calls standing_suggestions with the operator and counted_logins, the same call the REVIEW events make, and returns None for a pull request closed without merging. Traced by reading; the reviews it counts come from the entry refresh caches for every polled pull request.
A count of zero still produces a follow-up action, so every merged pull request with a fixer now gets one, even when nothing was deferred. The fixer then opens nothing and reports that.

groups.title: fix-pr follows up on a merged pull request
groups.kicker: A new skill section says how the fixer builds the follow-up
intro: The new "Follow up on a merged pull request" section has five steps: gather the candidates with project review suggestions plus any deferred ones, verify each against the current base, keep the ones that are clearly right and need neither the owner's decision nor a spec, build them as one change through implement's hand-over, and report.
The rest of the skill points at that section: the description, the opening, "Choose the pull request", the defer rule, the event list, the subagent's report, and the readiness report.
